area: Weft engine internals (@techery/weft-core + sdk, store-fs, index-sqlite): journaling, replay/salvage, budget, concurrency, HITL, projections, schema boundary, isolation/patches, sub-workflows, storage

features.name: Append-only journal as the only source of truth
features.description: A run is a sequence of {i, at, ev} records; every other artifact (state.json, tree.json, report.md, the sqlite index) is a fold over it. The event union covers run lifecycle (run.created/status/completed/failed/cancelled), steps (step.scheduled/attempt/completed/failed), humans (human.requested/answered/rejected), signals (signal.received/rejected), timers, patches (captured/merged/discarded), scope.violation, checks, notes, drops, budget.sampled, phase, log, and replay.salvaged/diverged.

features.name: Canonical-JSON step identity hashing
features.description: Step identity is sha256 over canonicalJson({kind, payload, schema, key}) with recursively sorted object keys, undefined-valued properties dropped, and Dates ISO-stringified. Including the explicit key in the hash keeps two same-content steps with different keys from serving each other's journal entries.

features.name: ReplayIndex: journal folded into serve-able entries
features.description: fromRecords builds bySeq/byHash/byKey completion maps, human entries by hash and id, incomplete scheduled entries by hash, buffered signals by name, plus totalUsage {tokens,usd,samples} accumulated from step.completed, step.attempt (failed prior attempt's spend) and step.failed error.detail.usage, and mergedBaseTrees from patch.merged. human.answered records only the FIRST standing answer; human.rejected clears the slot so a replacement can fill it; signal.rejected consumes the delivery the failed step took.

features.name: Three-tier replay matching (fast path / salvage / --reuse key)
features.description: matchStep first tries the same seq with the same hash+kind, then any unconsumed same-hash+kind entry (salvage, journaling replay.salvaged), then — only under reuse mode "key" — an unconsumed entry with the same key. Anything unmatched re-runs live and journals replay.diverged while still inside history.

features.name: Keyless-ambiguity guard tied to a workflow version stamp
features.description: run.created stores bodyHash = sha256(name + def.run.toString()) and optionally the host's bundle defHash. On resume versionUnchanged() requires both available stamps to agree; when they don't, positionsTrusted=false and a keyless step whose content matches more than one journaled entry re-runs (journaling replay.diverged with an "ambiguous keyless identity" reason) rather than taking the entry sitting at its seq.

features.name: OrderedDelivery: journaled completion ordering with a machine-independent stall watchdog
features.description: While replay is pure (no live dispatch yet), cached completions are parked and released in journaled completion order so seq numbers and continuations reproduce. A stall is detected by counting drained event-loop TURNS (3) with busy()==0 rather than wall-clock, then skipping forward; the first live dispatch calls breakOrder() and flushes everything.

features.name: verifyServe: refusing journaled effects whose result no longer holds
features.description: A StepSpec may supply verifyServe(journaled); a false verdict consumes the entry, journals replay.diverged, and re-executes with io.reExecuting=true (so recovery paths may treat an existing branch/tag as their own prior work rather than a collision). Used by git.commit (ancestor-of-HEAD check), git.checkout (HEAD still on the ref, branch-vs-detached aware), git.tag (tag peels to the journaled sha), branch.create (+checkout still current), ctx.integrate (tree hash / reverse-apply / mergedBaseTrees / forward-apply), function checks, and sub-workflow steps.

features.name: Generic step runner with retry, per-attempt abort, and deadline anchoring
features.description: runStep journals step.scheduled (hash, kind, key, label, phase, parentSeq via AsyncLocalStorage, route, scope, payload, childRunId), then loops attempts with a fresh AbortController each time; failures journal step.failed unless retryable (never for cancelled/budget_exceeded/gate_denied/human_denied), retries journal step.attempt carrying the failed attempt's usage and back off linearly. reuseIncomplete re-adopts a prior incomplete schedule so a resumed timed wait gets only the REMAINDER of its deadline.

features.name: Step timeout with bounded drain and late-usage harvest
features.description: withTimeout arms a referenced timer chunked below Node's 2^31-1ms ceiling, aborts the attempt on expiry, then races the losing promise against a 5s drain so a provider settling inside that window can hand back its accumulated Usage; the timeout StepError carries that usage so a later resume restores the charge.

features.name: Budget accounting: token+USD ledger with parent-linked child pools
features.description: Budget.charge sums non-negative input+output tokens and usd and propagates up the parent chain (root counts chargedCalls); remainingTokens/remainingUsd take the min of own and ancestor headroom; checkBeforeStep throws BudgetExceededError once either axis hits zero. Child budgets are created by fraction of remaining or absolute caps and always parent-linked.

features.name: Concurrency-aware budget admission (reserveCall)
features.description: Before dispatching a provider call, reserveCall parks rather than refuses: admits() requires (inflight+1) * (spent/samples) to fit in the remaining headroom, serializes calls one at a time while no cost sample exists, and wakes every parked caller whenever a charge lands or a call releases. It only throws when waiting cannot help (pool exhausted, or nothing in flight and this call still doesn't fit).

features.name: Budget restore across resumes and descendant journals
features.description: Resume restores max(sum of journaled usage, last budget.sampled) — the sample is a lower bound covering a crash between charge and terminal record — plus a recursive walk of parentage-verified descendant journals for child spend the parent's own roll-ups don't represent (clamped at zero per child), with a matching samples count so the per-call average stays honest. Re-entering a child restores the delta up the chain and restoreLocal()s the full amount into the fresh child ledger.

features.name: Pricing table and USD-only ceiling guard
features.description: When a provider reports tokens but no usd, the engine prices the call from config.providers[id].prices[model] or the built-in DEFAULT_PRICES (claude-opus-5/sonnet-5/haiku-4-5) and journals a budget.sampled after each charge. A run with a USD-only ceiling whose provider neither reports usd nor has configured pricing is refused before dispatch instead of silently running unbounded.

features.name: FIFO counting semaphore + per-provider limiters
features.description: Semaphore is a FIFO counting semaphore with abort-aware acquire; `with()` releases on settlement OR on abort (deliberately allowing a bounded overshoot rather than a permanent deadlock from a zombie step). The global limiter defaults to min(16, cpus-2) and wraps the entire agent lane (worktree creation included), exec/bash/fetch/check spawns; a per-provider Semaphore stacks on top for model calls.

features.name: HITL broker: human steps are journaled steps whose provider is a person
features.description: runHuman hashes {kind, question, detail, schema, risk, artifact, timeout settings}, matches a journaled request by hash, serves a standing answer (in journaled order) or re-surfaces the same request id and waits. Live requests journal human.requested with id h<N> (counter seeded from the journal's max), schema, risk, deadline, onTimeout policy and confirmToken.

features.name: Answer validation with a reject-and-reopen loop
features.description: An answer is checked against the step's authoritative Standard Schema (after unwrapping the {value} wire carrier); a failure from a human-submitted answer journals human.rejected, reopens the request, and waits for a replacement instead of failing the run. Out-of-process answers are structurally checked against the journaled JSON Schema before appending.

features.name: Answer delivery is serialized and CAS-guarded across processes
features.description: Engine.answer chains per runId::requestId, refuses journal-unsafe payloads, and appends via journal.appendIf under a re-fold loop: a standing answer, a terminal run event, or a lost CAS refuses the caller. A parent-addressed answer is routed to the live or durable descendant that actually holds the pending request (request ids are run-local).

features.name: Human deadlines with deny/escalate/default policies
features.description: A request with a timeout arms a referenced, chunked timer; at the deadline the policy applies — escalate logs and keeps waiting, default wraps and journals the pre-validated fallback, deny journals a {$timeout:"deny"} sentinel that becomes human_timeout for ask/review and {approved:false} for gates/approvals. The timeout append uses the same appendIf CAS as Engine.answer and abandons on a terminal event or a standing real answer. onTimeout.default is validated and JSON-checked at request time, not at the deadline.

features.name: Risk-tiered approval gates with typed confirmation
features.description: resolveApproval matches glob patterns over the gate action string first (picomatch, first match wins), then per-risk tiers, defaulting low→auto and everything else→ask; irreversible+ask additionally demands a confirm token `confirm:<sha256(action)[0:8]>` echoed in the answer, and a mismatch is treated as denied. Auto-approved gates append request+answer(answeredBy:"policy") in one batch and never wait.

features.name: In-agent permission hook and asks routed into the broker
features.description: Provider adapters get a ProviderHitl seam: onPermission escalates high/irreversible tool requests through the gate (deny by default when the attempt has been aborted), and onAsk opens a human "ask" step. Both are fenced against zombie attempts so an abandoned attempt cannot open gates or journal requests.

features.name: Signal waits: buffered, ordered, and rejection-consuming
features.description: ctx.signal is a journaled step with reuseIncomplete (so a resumed timed wait keeps its original deadline). takeOrAwaitSignal drains journaled signal.received entries first, then in-process buffered deliveries, then parks as a durable wait. A payload that fails the schema journals signal.rejected so a resume cannot re-take the same bad payload ahead of a corrected one. Delivery happens only via the owning engine's journal tailer, so a payload is never delivered twice.

features.name: Suspension model and tree-aggregated outcome()
features.description: Steps toggle between live work and durable waits (markWaiting/unmarkWaiting); a run is suspended when inflightLive==0 and pending waits exist. suspensionOf recursively folds live children so a parent whose only work is a child waiting on a person reports waiting_for_human and surfaces the child's pending requests; a waitBridge flips the parent's workflow step per level.

features.name: Projections: state / tree / report as pure folds
features.description: reduceState replays every event into RunState (steps with duplicate seqs across resume passes all retained, checks keyed by the schedule they belong to, terminal events clearing their opposite, first-standing-answer semantics matching replay). renderTree nests by parentSeq into phases with a "(no phase)" bucket; renderReport emits status/cost, outcome JSON, changes (including captured-but-not-integrated warnings), a checks table, ledger notes, failures & drops, remaining risk, and the exact `weft answer` command for the first pending request.

features.name: Snapshot publication ordered by covered record count
features.description: RunState carries `records` (how many journal records the reduction covered); the engine serializes snapshots per run on a promise chain and re-reduces index-sorted records each pass, and both the memory and fs stores refuse to publish a reduction covering fewer records than the standing one (the fs store does the compare under a cross-process snapshot.lock and writes each file tmp+rename).

features.name: Schema boundary: Zod→JSON Schema with primitive wrapping and lints
features.description: toWireSchema converts Zod via z.toJSONSchema({io:"input", reused:"inline"}), strips $schema, and wraps any non-object root as {value} (required, additionalProperties:false) because providers demand an object root; wrap/unwrap happens symmetrically on the way back. Depth >8 and non-zod vendors produce lints; non-zod schemas fall back to a permissive {value:{}} carrier.

features.name: Schema repair loop against the same provider session
features.description: runProviderWithRepair validates the unwrapped output against the real schema; on failure it appends a step.attempt ("schema repair n/max") and calls provider.repair(sessionId, req, issues) up to limits.repair (default 2) before throwing schema_repair_exhausted. Usage accumulates per turn with per-turn non-negative normalization, and every failure path carries the accumulated spend on the error so the journal record restores it later.

features.name: Structural JSON-Schema validator for hosts without the real schema
features.description: structuralCheck covers type (incl. unions and integer), enum, anyOf, required/properties, additionalProperties:false, array items, and the constraint keywords zod emits (const, minLength/maxLength/pattern, minimum/maximum/exclusive*, multipleOf with a scale-aware tolerance, minItems/maxItems), with order-independent deepEqual for enum/const.

features.name: JSON-safety gate on everything that crosses the journal
features.description: jsonUnsafeAt walks a value and names the first path JSONL cannot hold — undefined (including present-but-undefined properties), bigint, function, symbol, non-finite numbers, Map/Set/Date/class instances (realm-tolerant prototype test), and cycles via an ancestor stack that still allows diamond sharing. It gates workflow input, workflow output (before and after schema transforms), child input, answers, signal payloads, and onTimeout defaults.

features.name: Secret handles: redacted in the journal, resolved only on the live path
features.description: ctx.secret(name) returns {__weftSecret:name}; exec/bash env maps and fetch headers are journaled as `<redacted:NAME>` while resolveSecretValues reads process.env inside execute() only — so a journal-served step replays in an environment where the secret is gone, and a missing secret is an invalid_input StepError.

features.name: fetch: allow-list, manual redirect chain, and credential stripping
features.description: ctx.fetch checks config.fetchAllow (picomatch on hostname) on the live path only. When an allow-list exists or any header is secret-backed or credential-SHAPED (CREDENTIAL_HEADER regex), redirects are followed by hand: every hop is re-validated, only the five real redirect statuses are followed, max 5 hops, 303/POST-301/302 rewrite to GET dropping body and content-type/length, and crossing origins strips credential and secret-backed headers. Deadlines use a chunked AbortSignal that stays armed through the body read.

features.name: Write isolation: per-attempt worktrees seeded from the integration state
features.description: A step with `write` or isolation:"worktree" gets a worktree at tmpdir/weft-worktrees/<runId>/<seq>.<attempt>, pre-pruned (so a resume after a kill doesn't fail on a registered worktree) and seeded from integrationBaseCommit — a dangling, ref-pinned commit of the current tracked+untracked state, so later write agents build on earlier ctx.integrate() results rather than HEAD.

features.name: Patch capture, scope checking, and quarantine
features.description: capturePatch stages everything (force-adding in-scope but gitignored outputs), refuses accidental gitlinks, and diffs --cached --binary --no-renames --no-ext-diff --no-textconv with NUL-delimited paths. The engine unions captured files with provider-reported escaped paths (absolute or ../), runs checkScope, journals patch.captured plus scope.violation, and marks the patch quarantined when mode is strict.

features.name: In-place write-scope enforcement with ignored-tree manifests
features.description: An in-place writer (used by the merge-resolution agent) is bounded by tree snapshots before/after plus a listing diff of untracked-ignored entries and a content-hash stat manifest of pre-existing ignored paths (cap 10,000). Out-of-scope edits journal scope.violation and, in strict mode, are rolled back file-by-file from the snapshot (worktree-only restore, or rm for paths absent from the snapshot).

features.name: ctx.integrate: nested journaled snapshot/apply with conflict policies
features.description: Integration runs per patch as an outer step whose snapshot and apply are themselves journaled sub-steps (so a resume mid-ask reuses the PRE-conflict snapshot instead of capturing markers). Clean applies journal patch.merged with baseTree/resultTree; conflicts follow onConflict — "fail" restores and throws, "agent" runs a strict in-place resolver and verifies no conflict markers remain before accepting its self-report, "ask" (default) asks a person for skip/keep-conflicts/abort. A run that ends with un-integrated, un-discarded patches fails with unintegrated_patches.

features.name: Sub-workflows: own run, own journal, shared abort/agent-cap, scoped budget
features.description: ctx.workflow enforces maxDepth (default 3), never serves its completion (verifyServe:false) so the child's own journal is the replay authority, and reuses the journaled childRunId (from step.scheduled or the completed output) on re-execution. executeChildRun validates the child input schema on every execution, detects an 8-hex id collision with an unrelated journal and reallocates (up to 16 tries), launches the child with its own lease, and rolls the child's spend up onto the parent step as a delta beyond what earlier failed passes already carried.

features.name: Cross-process ownership: leases, fencing, and conditional terminals
features.description: acquireRun claims a run before execution (fs store: owner.json + TTL 15s under an owner.lock CAS); the engine renews every 5s and fences the runtime after a lost claim or 3 consecutive refresh failures. Fencing refuses all further appends, disarms deadline timers, rejects pending waits, and aborts step work WITHOUT journaling a terminal event. appendTerminal lands run.completed/failed/cancelled through appendIf so a cancellation committed in the tailer's blind spot converts the outcome instead of being overridden.

features.name: External-event tailer with retry-then-fence
features.description: The owning engine watches its own journal from launch and converts externally appended human.answered / signal.received / run.cancelled into in-process deliveries (structuredClone'd, idempotent against already-delivered ids). A watch that fails five times fences the run exactly like a lost lease, with exponential unref'd backoff in between.

features.name: Bounded cancel and non-terminal shutdown/detach
features.description: cancel() aborts, rejects human waits across the live descendant tree, and drains up to 5s; past the bound it journals run.cancelled BEFORE fencing, retires the active entry, and deliberately keeps the lease (a zombie may still be writing). shutdown() fences and drains every active run without journaling a terminal, releasing the claim only for runs that actually unwound — so runs stay resumable and a still-live one TTL-expires instead.

features.name: replay --dry: cost-free divergence report
features.description: replayDry re-executes the workflow against the journal with a runtime in dry mode: appends are synthesized in memory, matched steps are served, and the first would-run step throws a CancelledError recorded as a divergence. It reports hits, salvaged, diverged step refs, still-pending request ids, and whether the body completed.

features.name: Durable failure suppression for optional agent steps
features.description: With onError:"null" a StepError is recorded as a drop and a sentinel step.completed {$suppressed:true} is journaled for that seq, so a resume replays the same declared null instead of re-running the paid optional step; if the sentinel cannot be journaled the original error propagates rather than silently un-suppressing later.

features.name: Blob offload and repairable-vs-fatal read failures
features.description: Step outputs over limits.blobThresholdBytes (64KB, measured in real bytes) are replaced by {$outputBlob, size, preview}; transcripts, patches and review artifacts go to blobs directly. loadOutput returns undefined ONLY for BlobMissingError/BlobCorruptError/unparseable JSON — treated as a cache miss that re-runs the step — while any other store failure (EACCES/EIO/timeouts) propagates so a step is never re-paid to recover data that was never lost. FsBlobStore writes tmp+rename and verifies the sha256 of every read against the ref.

features.name: FsJournalStore: locked, fsynced JSONL appends with torn-tail recovery
features.description: Each append takes a cross-process lock (exclusive-create + 2.5s mtime renewal, 10s staleness with an identity-safe rename-aside steal, 30s acquisition deadline), reconciles on-disk growth into count/byteOffset twice (so a stolen lock's committed records are never truncated), re-tests the appendIf CAS, truncates only a genuinely torn trailing line, then loops writeSync to completion and fsyncs. Indices stay tentative until the bytes are durable.

features.name: Absence-vs-fault discipline throughout the fs store
features.description: Only ENOENT/ENOTDIR count as "no journal": read(), exists(), loadCache(), list() and the owner-claim reader all propagate EACCES/EIO instead of reporting a durable run as missing. list() skips only damaged (SyntaxError) or vanished runs so one corrupt journal cannot empty `weft ls` — or, through RunIndex.rebuild, delete healthy rows.

features.name: Freshness-checked run summaries and projection rebuild
features.description: summarize() prefers state.json but only while strictly newer than journal.jsonl (an equal mtime distrusts the projection), otherwise folds the journal; rebuildProjections() regenerates state.json, tree.json AND report.md from the journal for `weft doctor`-style repair.

features.name: SQLite run index: derived, self-healing, own-spend accounting
features.description: RunIndex keeps one row per run folded from its journal (status, timestamps, agentSteps, display tokens/usd, own tokens/usd, a lowercased search_text of workflow name, step keys/labels and human questions). PRAGMA user_version drift drops and recreates the table; a corrupt file (SQLITE_CORRUPT/NOTADB or a matching message) is deleted along with -wal/-shm and reopened, while SQLITE_BUSY/EACCES/EIO propagate. stats() sums own_tokens/own_usd so child spend is counted exactly once (workflow-kind roll-ups excluded, with seq→kind tracked chronologically because seqs restart on resume).

features.name: Error taxonomy: StepError with code, step ref, attempts, detail
features.description: Every step either returns a schema-validated value or throws a StepError carrying a StepErrorCode, a StepRef (seq/key/kind/label/runId), optional attempts and a detail bag (used to carry Usage across failures). BudgetExceededError and CancelledError are subclasses; serialize/deserialize round-trip through the journal, and isCancellation() is the single predicate fan-out uses to never swallow an abort.

features.name: Fan-out primitives: parallel, pipeline, ok()
features.description: ctx.parallel returns Settled[] in input order, caps items at limits.fanoutMax (4096) after settling already-running promise tasks, and rethrows any cancellation. ctx.pipeline builds immutable per-branch stage lists (step/filter/map) and runs lanes through mapWithConcurrency, dropping filtered lanes; ctx.ok narrows Settled[] to values and journals a `drop` for each failure.

features.name: Checks and the required-check gate
features.description: ctx.check supports exec checks (exit code, evidence tail-truncated to 2000 chars), fn checks (chunked timeout that yields a FAILED check rather than an aborted step, and never served from the journal), trustPrior records, and skipped records; a failing required check is collected and fails the run at the end with check_failed.

features.name: Journaled replacements for nondeterministic globals
features.description: ctx.now/random/uuid are journaled sideeffect steps so a replay reproduces the original values, and ctx.sleep is a durable timer step (reuseIncomplete, deadline anchored to the ORIGINAL schedule time, chunked past Node's timer ceiling, journaling timer.fired).

features.name: Agent-step caps and routing resolution
features.description: Agent dispatches are counted across the whole run tree (restored on resume from journaled agent step.scheduled records plus descendant journals): passing agentGuideline (15) logs once, passing agentHard (1000) throws. Routing resolves step opts → workflow defaults → engine config, and a default model applies only when the step actually routes to the provider that default was written for.

features.name: Test hooks seam
features.description: TestHooks lets @techery/weft-testing stub git ops, exec/bash, fetch, and env reads; a hook returning a value short-circuits the live path and the result is journaled exactly as a real side effect would be.

limitations.what: IntegrateOptions.order?: "sequential" is declared in the public API but never read — integration is unconditionally sequential (a for-of over results).

Two declared StepErrorCodes are never produced anywhere in packages/*/src: `max_turns` and `git_failed`. A GitError from the git layer becomes code "internal" via StepError.from. `human_denied` appears only in the retry predicate and is never thrown.

structuralCheck (the only validator hosts have for out-of-process answers) ignores allOf/oneOf/not/$ref/format/uniqueItems/patternProperties, tuple-form items, and non-false additionalProperties — so an answer can pass the wire check and still be rejected by the owning runtime, which is why the reject-and-reopen loop exists.

Any non-Zod Standard Schema degrades to a permissive {value:{}} wire schema, so the provider receives no shape guidance at all and the repair loop can only fire after the fact against the real schema.

Human steps have no `key` and no ambiguity guard: their identity hash is hashStep("human", payload) with no key or schema argument, and matchHuman returns the first unconsumed same-hash entry. Two identical questions in one workflow are distinguished only by occurrence order, with no positionsTrusted-style protection when the script changed.

replayDry does not compute positionsTrusted, ignores opts.defHash, and resets the budget and agent counter to empty — so its report can differ from what an actual resume of an edited script would do (which is exactly the case the tool is for).
limitations.evidence: packages/core/src/engine.ts:1792-1827 (no positionsTrusted / defHash / restore, `budget: new Budget({})`, `agentCounter: { count: 0 }`)

limitations.what: ctx.parallel's `concurrency` option is silently ignored unless EVERY task is a thunk; promise-form tasks fall through to Promise.all with no lane cap.
pipeline.run() defaults to concurrency = items.length, i.e. no pipeline-level cap; only the global limiter inside effectful steps bounds actual work.

Semaphore.with releases its permit on abort as well as settlement, so the configured concurrency cap can be exceeded by the number of timed-out-but-still-running steps (an accepted trade documented in the code).

Budget admission is a heuristic, not a guarantee: it uses the observed average cost per charged call and undercounts in-flight calls for zombie attempts, so the hard ceiling can be overshot by an in-flight call's actual cost — enforcement is after the fact in charge()/checkBeforeStep.

Resume-time spend restoration relies on the last durable budget.sampled as a lower bound; a crash after a provider charge but before both the terminal record and any sample loses that spend, and the sampled append is best-effort (`void rt.append`, `.catch(() => undefined)`).

Secret redaction covers only env maps and fetch header names/values passed as SecretHandles. Step OUTPUTS are journaled verbatim — exec/bash stdout+stderr, fetch response bodies and headers, agent prompts, and ctx.env.get's actual value all land in the journal unredacted.
Run ids are 8 hex characters of a UUID. start() only refuses an id whose journal already exists; collision detection and regeneration exist solely for CHILD runs (16 attempts, parentage-verified).

MemoryJournalStore claims never expire ("in one process a claim never goes stale"), so an in-process owner that dies without releasing blocks resume forever; MemoryBlobStore performs no hash verification on read, unlike FsBlobStore.
Strict completion ordering on replay ends at the first live dispatch, and a stall is resolved by skipping forward after 3 quiet drained turns — determinism of the remainder is explicitly best-effort.

Step timeouts cannot stop a runaway execution: withTimeout aborts, drains 5s, then fails the step while the zombie may keep running and mutating files; ctx.check's fn timeout is likewise best-effort (JS cannot force-kill the callback).

Most git write ops have no idempotency verifier, so a resume serves them from the journal without re-checking the world: add, fetch, pull, push, reset, apply, branch.delete, stash.push/pop/drop, clean, and checkout --discard (explicitly excluded).
verifyServe is disabled entirely whenever testHooks are configured, so fixture-driven runs never exercise the effect-still-holds re-check.
In-place scope verification of ignored content is capped at 10,000 files: a strict scope refuses to run (or fails mid-step) past the cap, and in warn mode edits beyond it are simply not seen.
A strict in-place step that modifies pre-existing gitignored files cannot roll them back (no snapshot holds ignored content) — it throws scope_violation and leaves the edit on disk.

Sub-workflow steps and function checks are never served from the journal (verifyServe: async () => false), so every resume re-enters the child run / re-runs the check function; the child's own journal is what avoids re-paying for its steps.

The sqlite index is never updated incrementally by the engine — nothing in core calls indexRun; the only host path is a full RunIndex.rebuild(), so rows are stale between rebuilds. search() is an unranked LIKE substring scan (no FTS) with a default limit of 50.

ctx.fetch allows every host unless fetchAllow is explicitly configured (the field is optional and undefined by default), and the manual per-hop validation path is skipped entirely when no allow-list and no credential-shaped header is present.

JournalStore.appendIf and acquireRun are optional; a store without them makes Engine fall back to unconditional appends and no ownership guard, explicitly accepting the answer/cancel/terminal races ("single-process hosts don't race themselves").

The fs append lock is best-effort: a holder frozen past the 10s stale threshold (SIGSTOP, VM pause) can have its lock stolen, and acquisition gives up after 30s with an error. Correctness then rests on the double reconcile + mutex.held() re-checks rather than on true mutual exclusion.
There is no blob garbage collection or deletion: BlobStore exposes only put/get/getText/has, so transcripts, patches and artifacts accumulate indefinitely under .weft/blobs.

The engine's own version stamp is sha256(name + def.run.toString()), so an edit inside an imported helper the workflow delegates to is invisible unless the host also supplies a bundle defHash; child runs never have a bundle stamp at all and inherit the root's verdict.
A duplicate explicit step key is only logged, not rejected — two steps sharing a key still both run and both become byKey candidates for `--reuse key`.

Cosmetic events (phase, log, drop) are suppressed during replay until the first live dispatch, so a resumed run's projections can lack logs/drops the first pass recorded only if that pass never journaled them; and setStatus/log/phase appends are fire-and-forget (`void this.append`), unobserved on failure.
After a bounded cancel or shutdown drain, the ownership lease is deliberately NOT released; the run stays claimed until its TTL expires, so another process cannot take it over promptly.

area: Developer-facing surface of weft: CLI (all 14 commands + flags), MCP server tools, daemon HTTP API + web UI, determinism gate (rules/bundler/sandbox/registry), host assembly + config format, testing harness, scaffolding, doctor, packaging/release, CI

features.name: `weft` program shell and global flags
features.description: Commander program built by `buildProgram(io)` with every line routed through an injectable `CliIo` writer, so the whole CLI is drivable from a test with no terminal. Two global options: `--cwd <dir>` (repo root, defaults to `process.cwd()`) and `--mock` (wires the fixture provider instead of Claude/Codex). Errors from any command are caught at the top and turned into one red line plus `process.exitCode = 1` — never `process.exit`, so journal writes flush.

features.name: `weft run <ref>` — start a run

features.name: AgentProvider contract
features.description: The frozen provider interface: `id`, `capabilities()`, `run(req, ctl)`, `repair(sessionId, req, errors, ctl)`. AgentRequest carries prompt, cwd, an already object-wrapped JSON Schema, label/key, model, effort, maxTurns, timeoutMs, onMaxTurns, a ToolPolicy (`allowEdits` + `deny[]`), an optional writeScope (paths/mode/also), and a `hitl` pair of engine callbacks. AgentResult returns raw `output` (never trusted — the engine validates), `usage`, optional `sessionId`, `transcript`, `filesTouched`. ProviderCapabilities declares `structured: "native"|"tool"`, `permissionHook`, `sessionResume`, `reportsUsd`.

features.name: ProviderRegistry
features.description: A Map keyed by provider id with register/get/has/ids. `get` on an unknown id throws naming the registered set. The host registers exactly three ids in live mode (claude, codex, mock) and, in mock mode, binds one shared MockAgentBuilder to all three ids so routing defaults still resolve.

features.name: Store conformance suites (the only conformance suite in the repo)
features.description: `journalStoreConformance` asserts monotonic per-run indices continuing across batches, run independence, `read(fromIndex)` resumption, `watch` replaying history then seeing a live append, `list` filtering by workflow/status/limit, optional `readSnapshot` round-trip that never replaces the journal, and `exists`. `blobStoreConformance` asserts put/get/getText/has round-trips for strings and bytes, content addressing (same bytes → same 64-hex ref, idempotent re-put), and that a missing ref reports absent and throws /not found/. It is exported from a separate subpath (`@techery/weft-testing/conformance`) so vitest is not a runtime dep of `runWorkflow`.

features.name: Claude adapter — structured output as a terminating sdk-mcp tool
features.description: An sdk-mcp server named `weft` serves one tool `structured_output` (model sees `mcp__weft__structured_output`) whose description embeds the step's JSON Schema. Its `result` parameter is deliberately declared `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` — an untyped parameter makes models stringify their answer — while staying permissive about contents because validation is the engine's job. Every prompt gets an appended `## Output` section restating the schema and that prose is not an answer. The handler boxes the value (`{value}`) so a legitimate null/undefined still counts as captured; a string `result` is defensively JSON.parsed, otherwise passed through untouched.

features.name: Claude adapter — finalize turn, repair, and paid-failure accounting
features.description: If the stream ends with nothing captured and `onMaxTurns === "finalize"`, one extra `query()` resumes the same session with FINALIZE_PROMPT; still nothing captured throws `agent finished without calling structured_output`. `repair()` re-prompts the same session with a bulleted `path: message` issue list plus the schema; a missing sessionId falls back to a full `run()`. The no-output Error is `Object.assign`-ed with the turn's `usage` so the engine folds already-burned spend into the failure record.

features.name: Claude adapter — session/resume, usage and transcript extraction
features.description: `session_id` is absorbed from any SDK message that carries a non-empty one and stored on the Turn; a repair or finalize turn passes it as `Options.resume`. Usage comes only from `result` messages and accumulates across turns of one step: `usage.input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` (emitted only when >0), and `total_cost_usd` summed with a `usdSeen` flag so a missing cost is absent rather than 0. Transcript lines are `assistant: <text>`, `assistant → tool: <name>`, `result: <subtype>`; `filesTouched` is populated by the gate's `onEdit` callback (deduped).

features.name: Claude adapter — abort and long-deadline handling
features.description: Each `stream()` builds a fresh AbortController, aborts it immediately if `ctl.signal` is already aborted, otherwise mirrors the abort once; the listener is removed in `finally`. The step deadline arms in chunks of at most 2_147_483_647 ms because Node clamps a longer single timer to ~1 ms (a 30-day agent would abort instantly); the timer is cleared in `finally`. `permissionMode` is pinned to `"default"` because canUseTool is only consulted there.

features.name: Claude tool gate — edit-tool and write-scope enforcement
features.description: `createToolGate` returns a `CanUseTool`. The terminating tool is never gated. `tools.deny` matches both the bare and fully-qualified names. EDIT_TOOLS = {Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit} are denied outright on a read-only step. With a scope, the edit's `file_path`/`notebook_path` is resolved to a posix cwd-relative path and tested with `scopeMatcher` — the SAME predicate the post-hoc `checkScope` uses, deliberately shared so the live gate cannot drift back to picomatch's fail-open array semantics. Strict mode denies: an out-of-scope path, an undeterminable target path, and an in-scope path whose deepest existing ancestor `realpath`s outside the worktree (dangling symlinks followed by hand, depth-capped at 8). Warn mode lets the edit land for post-hoc flagging.

features.name: Claude tool gate — Bash screening
features.description: Four layers. (1) Any command matching /\bgit\b/ is rewritten with GIT_READ_WRAPPER prepended — a shell function forcing `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` on diff/log/show, `--no-textconv` on blame, `-c core.fsmonitor=false` and `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` on every git call — applied on write steps too. (2) Read-only steps are deny-by-default: `isReadOnlyCommand` tokenizes with a hand-written shell-word resolver that returns null on any expansion/substitution/redirection/unterminated quote, then requires every segment head to be a bare (non-path-qualified) name in a fixed READ_COMMANDS allow-list or a git read subcommand, and refuses PATH/LD_*/GIT_* env prefixes plus per-command escape options (`git --output`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`, `--show-signature`, `grep -O`, `find -exec/-delete/-fprint*`, `rg --pre`, `diff -l`, `tree -o`, `file -C`, `date -s`, `sort -o/--compress-program`, `printf -v`, `uniq`/`xxd` second positional). (3) Strict write scope additionally denies absolute/`~`/`$HOME` paths, `..` traversal, any `$`/backtick/process-substitution token, any literal word resolving out of the worktree, and any git subcommand in SHARED_GIT_METADATA_SUBCOMMANDS (config, remote, branch, tag, checkout, switch, stash, notes, fetch, pull, worktree, gc, prune, update-ref, symbolic-ref, reflog, filter-branch, replace, maintenance) — then brokers EVERY non-provably-read-only command at risk `high`. (4) `isRiskyCommand` routes push/publish/deploy/apply-style commands (including plumbing `send-pack`/`http-push`, `-c alias.*`/`--config-env=alias.*` definitions, `eval`, computed heads, and any git subcommand outside KNOWN_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS) to the HITL broker at risk `high`.

features.name: Codex adapter — native structured output with vendor schema adaptation
features.description: The step's schema is passed as `TurnOptions.outputSchema`; the final message is the JSON value. `toStrictSchema` walks only real JSON-Schema keyword positions (SCHEMA_KEYWORDS / SCHEMA_LIST_KEYWORDS / SCHEMA_MAP_KEYWORDS) so `const`/`default`/`enum`/`examples` literals pass through byte-for-byte, then sets `additionalProperties: false` on every object schema that doesn't already carry a meaningful catchall, and rewrites `required` to list every property (OpenAI strict-mode requirement; Zod omits defaulted keys). `parseOutput` tries a direct JSON.parse, then a ```json fence, then returns the raw string so the engine's schema check fails it and repair gets a turn instead of the work being discarded.

features.name: Codex adapter — sandbox as the only live guard
features.description: There is no per-tool hook. `ThreadOptions` pins `workingDirectory: req.cwd`, `sandboxMode: allowEdits ? "workspace-write" : "read-only"`, `skipGitRepoCheck: true` (the engine already chose the dir), `approvalPolicy: "never"` (no TTY exists), plus model and `modelReasoningEffort` (Weft's five effort tiers are a subset of the SDK's names). `capabilities()` reports `permissionHook: false`, and `filesTouched` is deliberately returned as `[]` so the engine's worktree diff is the sole authority on what changed.

features.name: Codex adapter — session/resume, usage, abort
features.description: `run()` calls `startThread()`; `repair()` calls `resumeThread(sessionId, …)` with the same thread options and a repair prompt listing the schema issues, falling back to a fresh `run()` when no thread id was ever reported. `thread.id` is copied to `sessionId` only when it is a non-empty string. Usage maps `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cached_input_tokens` (cacheRead only when >0); `usd` is deliberately never set — the engine prices from config. Abort is bracketed: an already-aborted signal throws `aborted` before the SDK is touched, and a turn that finished after cancellation is discarded rather than returned. `turnSignal` combines ctl.signal with the step deadline via `AbortSignal.any`, chunking deadlines over the Node timer ceiling with `unref()` and a `done()` released in `finally` so a successful long-timeout turn does not pin its timer.

features.name: Codex transcript rendering
features.description: `renderTranscript` maps ThreadItems to one line each in production order: `assistant:`/`reasoning:` (trimmed, empty dropped), `exec (<status|exit N>): <command>`, `files (<status>): <kind> <path>, …`, `mcp (<status>): <server>.<tool>`, `search: <query>`, `todo: <done>/<total>`, `error: <message>`. Unknown item types are skipped rather than rendered as [object Object]. An absent/empty list renders "".

features.name: Mock provider — scripted fixtures
features.description: `mock()` builds a MockAgentBuilder holding rules and a shared call log; `.provider(id)` mints a MockProvider sharing them. A rule matches on `key` (glob where `*` crosses `/`, so `review:*` matches `review:src/a.ts`), `label` (same glob), and `prompt` (substring or RegExp), honouring an optional `times` budget; no match throws an error listing every registered rule. Responders may be a function of the MockRequest or a literal. Options can write files into the request cwd, delay (abortable via ctl.signal), override usage (default `{input:100, output:50}`), and set `filesTouched` explicitly (default: the `writes` keys) to model paths patch capture cannot see. Session ids are `mock-<id>-<n>`; `repair()` looks up the original request by session id and computes its attempt number from the call log. Capabilities mirror Claude's (tool/true/true/true).

features.name: Typed git API surface (ctx.git)
features.description: Reads (journaled, no approval): status, head, branches, mergeBase, changedSince, diff, log, show, blame, fileAt, snapshot. Writes (journaled, gated): add, commit, checkout, fetch, pull, push, reset, apply, tag, branch.create/delete, stash.push/pop/drop, clean. Every write accepts `GitWriteOpts.risk` to RAISE (never lower) its fixed tier. `tag()` returns the peeled COMMIT sha so resume can detect a `tag -f` re-point.

features.name: Git risk tiers
features.description: A fixed table maps 18 write op names to Risk: low = add, commit, branch.create, checkout, fetch, stash.push, stash.pop, tag; medium = pull, reset, apply, stash.drop, checkout.discard; high = push; irreversible = push.force, reset.hard, branch.delete, clean. `ctx` picks the op name dynamically (`opts.force ? "push.force" : "push"`, `mode === "hard" ? "reset.hard" : "reset"`, `discard ? "checkout.discard" : "checkout"`) and combines the table tier with the caller's via `maxRisk`, which only ever raises along [low, medium, high, irreversible].

features.name: Git CLI hardening (execution-safety of typed reads)
features.description: Every invocation runs `git -c core.fsmonitor=false …` (an fsmonitor hook is repository-configured code a journaled read must not execute) in a fixed cwd with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_PAGER=cat, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, LC_ALL=C and GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF REMOVED (undefined, not empty — an empty value is a command git tries to run). Every diff-family call adds `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`; `show` and `blame` too. Parsed commands add `-c core.quotePath=false` and use `-z` (porcelain=v2 status, name-status, name-only, ls-files, log records) so pathnames containing newlines/quotes/backslashes round-trip verbatim. `refArg` rejects empty or `-`-leading values in ref/name argv positions so `show("--output=/x")` cannot turn a read into a write.

features.name: git.snapshot() — gc-safe tree snapshot
features.description: Not `stash create` (which omits untracked files). A throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE is seeded `read-tree HEAD` (so a tracked-but-gitignored file stays in), then `add -A .`, `write-tree`; if the tree equals HEAD's tree it returns HEAD, otherwise `commit-tree … -p HEAD` with a fixed weft identity and the result is PINNED at `refs/weft/snapshots/<sha>` so `git gc --prune` cannot collect it across a long suspension. The temp index is removed in `finally`.

features.name: Worktree isolation
features.description: `addWorktree` mkdirs the parent, runs `git worktree add --detach <dir> <baseRef|HEAD>` in the repo root, then reads the sha back from inside the new worktree (baseRef may be a branch/tag). `removeWorktree` tries `git worktree remove --force`, and on failure rm -rf's the directory and runs `git worktree prune`, tolerating an already-removed dir. Engine-side, each write attempt gets `tmpdir()/weft-worktrees/<runId>/<seq>.<attempt>` (per-ATTEMPT so a retry never removes a directory a hung attempt still writes to), is pre-cleaned via removeWorktree (a process killed mid-step leaves the dir registered), and is seeded from `integrationBaseCommit(cwd)` — the CURRENT integration state including patches an earlier `ctx.integrate` left uncommitted — not from HEAD. Teardown runs in `finally` and never vetoes a paid, journaled result.

features.name: Patch capture
features.description: `capturePatch` stages everything (`add -A`), then force-adds any gitignored file that the declared scope patterns match (so a declared `dist/**` output is not lost with the worktree), lists `diff --cached --name-only --no-renames --no-ext-diff -z` (no rename detection: `git mv` out of scope would otherwise list only the destination and silently delete the out-of-scope source; -z keeps a newline filename one path), then emits `diff --cached --binary --no-renames --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`. `--binary` is what makes image/archive patches applicable at all. Before the diff, `refuseAccidentalGitlinks` inspects `--raw` for newly-introduced mode-160000 entries (oldMode ≠ 160000 so a removed submodule isn't misread), cross-checks against `.gitmodules`-registered paths, and throws naming the path rather than journaling a patch that applies cleanly and lands zero files.

features.name: Write-scope checking
features.description: `scopeMatcher(scope)` is the single predicate: patterns from `paths` + `also` are split into includes and `!`-prefixed excludes and compiled as TWO picomatch matchers (`dot: true`); a file is in scope iff it matches ≥1 include and 0 excludes. This exists because picomatch's array semantics fail open twice — `["src/**", "!src/secret.ts"]` reports secret.ts as a match, and `["!secrets/**"]` alone matches the whole tree. An empty/inclusion-free scope matches nothing. Paths and patterns are NFC-normalized (macOS hands back decomposed names) and newlines/CRs in paths are mapped to a stand-in character because picomatch's wildcards compile to classes that do not cross a newline. `checkScope` just partitions a file list with that predicate, preserving input order.

features.name: Quarantine semantics
features.description: After capture, `files` is the UNION of what the worktree diff saw and any provider-reported path that escaped it (`isAbsolute(path) || path.startsWith("../")`) — the escaped paths are the only witness for edits capture cannot see, and they can never match a repo-relative glob so they land out of scope by construction. `quarantined = scope.mode === "strict" && outOfScope.length > 0`. The PatchRef carries `{ref, key, files, quarantined?, outOfScope?}`; `patch.captured` and a `scope.violation` event are journaled (the violation is journaled even when every edit escaped and there is no patch to attach it to). A quarantined patch is never merged — `ctx.integrate` records it under `ledger.quarantined` and logs the out-of-scope files.

features.name: In-place write-scope enforcement (no worktree)
features.description: For `writeInPlace` steps (used by the `onConflict: "agent"` resolver), the engine snapshots the tree with `integrationBaseCommit`, lists gitignored entries (`ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory -z`), and builds a sha256 CONTENT manifest of the pre-existing ignored tree (metadata is forgeable), capped at 10 000 files — a strict scope refuses to run rather than trust a truncated manifest. After the dispatch it re-diffs the two snapshots with `--no-renames -z`, re-lists new ignored entries, and re-walks the manifest. Out-of-scope files are journaled as `scope.violation`, and under strict mode are ROLLED BACK via `restorePatchFiles` and removed from the reported file list. Modified pre-existing IGNORED paths under strict mode throw `scope_violation` — no snapshot holds ignored content, so there is nothing to restore from.

features.name: applyPatchToTree — clean apply then 3-way
features.description: An empty/whitespace patch is a no-op success. Otherwise `git apply --check`; on success apply for real. On failure it falls back to `--3way`, but because `--3way` implies `--index` (which would stage the result and any pre-existing user edits into the CALLER's index) the merge runs against a throwaway GIT_INDEX_FILE seeded `read-tree HEAD` then `add -A .` — only the working tree keeps the result. Conflicts are reported from `diff --diff-filter=U -z` in the throwaway index; failing that, from four `git apply` stderr patterns (patch failed, does not apply/does not exist in index/No such file, already exists in working directory, binary without full index line); failing that, from the patch's own `---`/`+++` headers (handling `/dev/null` deletions and trailing-tab timestamps). The temp index is removed in `finally`.

features.name: ctx.integrate — merge orchestration and ledger
features.description: Iterates the results sequentially. A result with no patch → `ledger.skipped.push("(no patch)")`; a quarantined patch → `ledger.quarantined`. Otherwise one journaled `sideeffect` step per patch wraps TWO nested journaled steps — a snapshot step (`treeHash` + `integrationBaseCommit(cwd, patch.files)` force-adding the patch's own targets so even an ignored pre-existing collision file is restorable) and an apply step — so a resume mid-ask reuses the PRE-conflict snapshot and the first pass's outcome rather than snapshotting conflict markers and stacking a second apply. A successful apply appends `patch.merged {key, ref, baseTree, resultTree}` and lands in `ledger.merged`. The ledger is `{merged, conflicts, quarantined, skipped}` and run status is set to "integrating" for the duration.

features.name: ctx.integrate — resume idempotency check
features.description: `verifyServe` decides whether a journaled merge may be served on replay. A non-applied journal entry always serves. Otherwise: if the live tree hash equals the journaled `resultTree`, serve. Else fetch the patch blob and try `git apply --reverse --check` — success means the content is present (later patches moved the tree past it), serve. Else, if a LATER journaled merge started from this patch's `resultTree` (`replay.mergedBaseTrees`), serve — that later merge may have edited the very lines this patch introduced. Only if a FORWARD `git apply --check` succeeds (proving the tree genuinely lacks the patch) does the step re-execute.

features.name: ctx.integrate — the three conflict strategies
features.description: `onConflict` defaults to "ask". `"fail"`: restore the patch's files from the pre-conflict snapshot, throw StepError("conflict", …) naming the conflicted files. `"agent"`: spawn an in-place, STRICT-scoped agent step keyed `merge:<patchKey>` whose scope is exactly `applied.conflicts`, asking it to resolve every marker and touch nothing else; the model's `resolved: true` self-report is NOT trusted — `conflictMarkersIn` re-reads each file and matches /^<{7}(?: |$)/m, and only a clean result journals `patch.merged {conflicted: true}`; otherwise the patch's files AND the conflicted files are restored and a StepError("conflict") names whether the agent gave up or lied. `"ask"`: a journaled human ask with enum {skip, keep-conflicts, abort} — keep-conflicts journals `patch.merged {conflicted: true}` and lands markers, skip restores and reports `applied: false` (→ ledger.skipped), abort restores and throws. Ledger placement: conflicted merges → `ledger.conflicts`, unapplied → `ledger.skipped`.

features.name: ctx.discard
features.description: Collects PatchRefs from the passed results, and in one journaled `sideeffect` step appends a `patch.discarded {key, ref}` event per patch and marks each in-memory patch state `discarded`. A call with no patches is a no-op.

features.name: restorePatchFiles — rollback discipline
features.description: Per file: probe `git cat-file -e <snapRef>:<path>` and distinguish genuine absence (exit 1, or "does not exist in"/"exists on disk, but not in" in stderr) from a repository/object-store error, which throws `exec_failed` rather than being misread as absence (which would delete a tracked file). Present → `git restore --worktree --source <snapRef> -- <file>` (worktree-only, so a caller's staged index is not destroyed). Absent → `rm -rf` the path (recursive so a new ignored DIRECTORY entry rolls back whole). Every rollback op must succeed — a swallowed failure would leave a skipped integration on a half-applied patch.

features.name: stdlib: adversarialVerify
features.description: For each claim, `refuters` (default DEFAULT_REFUTERS = 3, clamped by `positiveInt`) independent agent steps get a prompt that explicitly instructs `refuted=true` when uncertain. All claim×refuter promises are created eagerly and handed to `ctx.parallel`, then read from `settled[i * refuters + r]`. A claim dies at `Math.floor(refuters/2) + 1` refute votes — a STRICT majority, so a 1-of-2 tie never kills. Settled entries are used deliberately instead of `ctx.ok`: a refuter branch that FAILED counts as a refute vote (`refuter R failed (<code>): <message>`), so a claim never survives because nobody could check it. Keys default to `refute:<claimIndex>:<refuterIndex>`, overridable via `keyFor`. An empty claim list short-circuits. Returns `{survived, refuted: [{claim, reasons}]}` plus a summary `ctx.log`. `adversarialVerifyResultSchema(claim)` mints the matching output schema.

features.name: stdlib: judgePanel
features.description: One attempt per angle (keys `attempt:<i>`, optionally `keyPrefix`-namespaced), then ONE JUDGE PER SURVIVING ATTEMPT (keys `judge:<i>`) — the judge count is derived, not configurable. Zero angles throws StepError("invalid_input"); all attempts failing throws StepError("internal"). Failed attempts are dropped via `ctx.ok`, and the judge schema is pinned to the surviving count with `judgeVerdictSchema(n)`: `scores` array of exactly n numbers in [0,10], `best` an int in [0, n-1], plus a rationale — so a wrong-length verdict triggers schema repair. Tally: mean score per attempt over finite scores only, plus best-vote counts (out-of-range `best` ignored). Winner = most best-votes, ties broken by higher mean; every judge failing falls back to attempt 0 with an explicit log. Returns `{winner, attempts, scores}`.

features.name: stdlib: loopUntilDry
features.description: Pure bookkeeping around a caller-supplied `find(round)`: it spawns no steps itself. `dryRounds` (default 2) and `maxRounds` (default 10) both go through `positiveInt`, so NaN would otherwise run zero rounds and Infinity would remove the paid-round ceiling. Each round's items are deduped by `keyOf` against a Set of everything ever seen; `added === 0` increments a dry streak (reset by any new item), and the loop returns when the streak reaches `dryRounds` or the round ceiling is hit. Every round logs `returned N, M new (K unique so far)`, and both exit paths log which one fired.

features.name: stdlib: completenessCritic
features.description: A single agent step (key defaults to `completeness`, overridable) whose prompt forbids reviewing quality/style/correctness and enumerates the gap classes to hunt: a modality never run, a claim asserted but unverified, a source referenced but unread, a question left unanswered, a scope quietly narrowed. `instructions` is optional — without it the prompt tells the critic to infer intent from the work. Returns `{missing: [{what, why}]}` and logs the gap count.

features.name: stdlib: multiModalSweep
features.description: One agent step per lens, keyed `sweep:<mode.name>` (optionally `keyPrefix`-namespaced) and run through `ctx.parallel`. Each lens's prompt names the OTHER lenses so the agent knows breadth buys nothing. An empty mode list short-circuits to []. Failures are dropped via `ctx.ok` (which records the drop) and the dropped mode names are logged. Returns `[{mode, result}]` in mode order for the survivors; `sweepResultSchema(result)` mints the matching output schema.

features.name: stdlib: finalReport
features.description: Synchronous, agent-free, deterministic markdown assembly: `# <title.trim()>` then, per section, `## <heading.trim()>` and the trimmed body (omitted entirely when empty), joined with blank lines and terminated by a newline. Takes `ctx` only to emit one log line. Byte-for-byte stable so reports diff cleanly between runs and the last step of a workflow spends no tokens on formatting.

features.name: stdlib: shared internals
features.description: `routing(opts)` forwards only the routing keys actually supplied (provider/model/effort) so step and workflow defaults still win; `prefixed(prefix, key)` composes `<prefix>:<key>` so two uses of one pattern in a workflow cannot claim the same keys; `positiveInt(value, fallback)` clamps to a finite positive integer; `asPromptJson` renders values with 2-space JSON for prompts. Nothing is exported from the package root.

features.name: Engine-side repair loop and usage accounting around providers
features.description: `runProviderWithRepair` calls `provider.run`, then loops: unwrap the wire value, validate against the REAL schema, and on failure call `provider.repair(result.sessionId, req, issues, …)` until `repairMax` (config default 2) is exceeded, then throw `schema_repair_exhausted`. Usage accumulates across every turn — including turns preceding a failure — with each turn's components clamped positive per-turn so a malformed negative cannot subtract earlier real spend, and a provider error's duck-typed `.usage` is folded into the StepError detail. Cost is filled in from the config price table when the provider reports no USD; a run with a USD-only ceiling, a provider with `reportsUsd: false`, and no configured price is REFUSED before dispatch.

features.name: Engine-side HITL bridge for provider permission asks
features.description: The `hitl.onPermission` the engine hands each provider gates only `high` and `irreversible` risk through `rt.gateStep` (action `agent tool <tool> (<label>)`, detail = first 500 chars of the JSON input), auto-allowing lower tiers. Both `onPermission` and `onAsk` are fenced against zombie attempts: an aborted step's signal makes onPermission deny with "attempt aborted" and onAsk throw CancelledError, so an abandoned attempt cannot open a gate or journal a human request the run will never answer.

limitations.what: There is NO AgentProvider conformance suite. `@techery/weft-testing/conformance` ships only `journalStoreConformance` and `blobStoreConformance`; nothing asserts that a new provider implements structured output, repair, session resume, abort, or usage extraction consistently. Each adapter is verified by its own bespoke test file instead (claude.test.ts ~40 cases, codex.test.ts ~24), so the two adapters are tested against different expectations.

limitations.what: Only three provider ids exist anywhere: claude, codex, mock. No OpenAI-direct, Gemini, Bedrock/Vertex, or local-model adapter. `ProviderId` is typed as `"claude" | "codex" | (string & {})`, so a third id typechecks but resolves to a registry miss at dispatch.

`ProviderHitl.onAsk` is dead contract surface. The engine implements and fences it, but no shipped adapter ever calls it — Claude's gate only calls `onPermission`, and Codex has no hook at all. Only `onPermission` is exercised.
limitations.evidence: packages/core/src/provider.ts:26 (declaration); packages/core/src/ctx.ts:522-533 (only implementation); grep across packages/*/src shows call sites only at packages/provider-claude/src/gate.ts:219,226 — both onPermission

limitations.what: The Codex adapter silently ignores several AgentRequest knobs: `maxTurns`, `onMaxTurns`, and `tools.deny` are never read (`threadOptions` passes only workingDirectory, sandboxMode, skipGitRepoCheck, approvalPolicy, model, modelReasoningEffort). It also always returns `filesTouched: []`, so a Codex write step outside a worktree has no adapter-side witness of what it touched.

Write-scope enforcement is asymmetric between providers. Claude enforces scope LIVE via canUseTool (strict denies out-of-scope edits, symlink escapes, shell writes, shared git-metadata mutations); Codex has no per-tool hook, so its only live guard is the coarse `workspace-write` sandbox and the scope is enforced purely post-hoc by the worktree diff. A strict scope therefore means materially different things per provider.

Codex reports tokens only, and the built-in price table contains claude models exclusively (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5). A run with a USD-only budget routed to Codex is refused at dispatch unless the host explicitly configures a price for that model.

`IntegrateOptions.order?: "sequential"` is inert — the field is never read anywhere in the engine. `integrate` always applies patches in array order in a plain `for` loop; there is no parallel or dependency-ordered integration.

limitations.what: The Claude gate's terminal clause allows every tool it does not specifically recognise. Anything that is not the terminating tool, not in `tools.deny`, not in EDIT_TOOLS, and not `Bash` — WebFetch/WebSearch, Task/subagent spawning, other MCP servers' tools — is unconditionally allowed even on a read-only step or under a strict write scope.

limitations.what: `warn`-mode write scope leaves the shell completely unscreened on a write step. The out-of-tree path, `..` traversal, computed-token, symlink-escape, shared-git-metadata and broker-everything checks are all gated on `scope?.mode === "strict"`; in warn mode only `isRiskyCommand` applies. Post-hoc patch capture cannot see anything written outside the worktree, so warn-mode escapes are recorded only if the provider self-reports them.
limitations.evidence: packages/provider-claude/src/gate.ts:192-224 (all four screens conditioned on strict); packages/core/src/ctx.ts:621-635 (escaped paths come only from `result.filesTouched`)

limitations.what: Escaped-path detection in the engine is posix-only: `isAbsolute(path) || path.startsWith("../")`. A Windows-style `..\\` relative escape reported by a provider would not be recognised as escaped and would not be forced out of scope.

Most git write ops have no resume verifier. Only `commit`, `checkout` (non-discard), `tag`, and `branch.create` pass a `verifyServe`; `add`, `fetch`, `pull`, `push`/`push.force`, `reset`/`reset.hard`, `apply`, `stash.push/pop/drop`, `branch.delete`, `clean`, and discard-checkouts are served from the journal on replay with no check that the effect still holds. Additionally, all verifiers are disabled whenever test hooks are installed.
limitations.evidence: packages/core/src/ctx.ts:1494 (`verifyServe && !rt.host.testHooks`), :1519-1524 (add: no verifier), :1576-1615 (fetch/pull/push/reset/apply: none), :1710-1730 (branch.delete/stash/clean: none), :1548-1551 (discard checkout deliberately unverified)

limitations.what: The GIT_READ_WRAPPER is prepended whenever the raw command text matches /\\bgit\\b/ — including when "git" appears only inside a quoted string or as an argument (`grep git README`). The prepended shell function definition is then injected into an unrelated command line.

The read-only Bash allow-list (READ_COMMANDS, READ_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS) is a hard-coded set with no configuration hook; a project's own read-only tooling cannot be added without editing the package. The design comment accepts the over-denial explicitly.

`judgePanel` has no way to set the judge count independently — it spawns exactly one judge per SURVIVING attempt, so panel size shrinks whenever an attempt fails and is 1 for a single angle. Judges also see all attempts in fixed index order with no anonymisation or order shuffling, so position bias is unmitigated.
limitations.evidence: packages/stdlib/src/judge.ts:118-129 (`attempts.map((_attempt, i) => …)`), :67-78 (attempts rendered in index order); packages/stdlib/src/judge.ts:38-45 (options carry no `judges` field)

limitations.what: `multiModalSweep` keys steps as `sweep:<mode.name>`; two modes sharing a name collide on the same step key, and nothing validates uniqueness. `adversarialVerify` likewise creates every claim×refuter promise eagerly and passes them to `ctx.parallel` with no `concurrency` option — a 100-claim × 3-refuter call issues 300 in-flight lanes bounded only by the global limiter and the `fanoutMax` cap (default 4096).
limitations.evidence: packages/stdlib/src/sweep.ts:79; packages/stdlib/src/adversarial.ts:88-104 (eager promise array), :104 (`ctx.parallel(tasks)` with no opts); packages/core/src/ctx.ts:938-951 (concurrency honoured only for thunk tasks); packages/core/src/config.ts:104 (fanoutMax 4096)

limitations.what: Three of the six stdlib patterns are thin. `finalReport` is 46 lines of pure string concatenation with no agent and no await. `loopUntilDry` (75 lines) spawns no steps at all — it is dedupe + streak bookkeeping around a caller-supplied `find`. `completenessCritic` (70 lines) is a single `ctx.agent` call with a fixed prompt and one optional key override. None of the six exposes retry, timeout, isolation, write-scope, or per-step `maxTurns` — only provider/model/effort routing is forwarded.
limitations.evidence: packages/stdlib/src/report.ts:36-46; packages/stdlib/src/loop.ts:36-75; packages/stdlib/src/critic.ts:58-70; packages/stdlib/src/internal.ts:8-21 (Routing is the entire forwarded option surface)

limitations.what: `toStrictSchema` unconditionally overwrites `required` with every property key of an object schema (documented as intentional for OpenAI strict mode). A schema that meant some fields optional is shown to the Codex model as all-required; correctness relies on the engine's later validation against the real schema plus repair.

In-place strict scope cannot be verified above 10 000 pre-existing ignored files — the step is refused up front with `invalid_input`, and a re-walk that crosses the cap after the step throws `scope_violation`. Edits inside pre-existing ignored paths are also unrecoverable: there is no snapshot holding ignored content, so a strict violation there fails the step rather than rolling back.

`capturePatch` and the mock provider's `filesTouched` are the only witnesses for out-of-worktree edits, and `capturePatch` by construction sees nothing outside the worktree. The Claude gate's `commandEscapesWorktree` is explicitly documented as a lexical screen, not a sandbox: a destination the shell computes at run time (or any behaviour internal to an invoked binary) is invisible to it.
